title: Dashboard Wireframe: Preemptive Capacity and Noise Reduction Heuristics
content:
Background:
This note outlines a compact observability surface and dashboard wireframe focused on two operational problems that routinely trigger expensive firefighting: 1) sudden token-serving bursts that exceed reserved capacity and 2) noisy trace/metric streams that hide signal during rollouts. Unlike broader SLI/SLO design docs, this is a practical sketch for a single-page operator dashboard + associated trace heuristics to enable preemptive mitigation and faster root cause isolation.

Objectives:
- Provide early warning for preemptive capacity actions (scale-up, fallback routing, canary pause).
- Surface high-fidelity signals while reducing noisy trace ingestion and query costs.
- Make drilldowns fast: one-click from anomalous panel to targeted trace slices and tenant-level panels.
- Keep panels lightweight to maintain query budget and usable at 5s refresh for active incident handling.

Primary user persona:
- Oncall SRE or runtime ops engineer reacting to latency/cost regressions during rollouts.
- Product/platform engineer validating rollout telemetry for a new model variant.

Key metric definitions (names, unit, collection notes):
- token_served_rate_per_min (float): tokens/sec aggregated to per-minute buckets; tag by model, route, tenant_id.
- request_50/90/99_latency_ms (int): p50/p90/p99 of request end-to-end latency including queueing; compute on ingesters to minimize series cardinality.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio (pct): hits/(hits+misses) measured at the serving host, tag by model and cache_key_prefix.
- fallback_rate (pct): fraction of requests routed away from primary model due to capacity or errors; tag by fallback_reason.
- preemptive_headroom_index (float): computed heuristic = (reserved_capacity_tokens_per_min - recent_5min_peak_tokens_per_min)/reserved_capacity_tokens_per_min; values < 0.15 flagged.
- tenant_cost_rpm (usd/min): estimated token cost per minute per tenant (approximate) used for billing-visible alerting.

Trace heuristics (what to collect, how to sample):
- Anchor spans: each request should create an anchor span with stable tags: request_id, tenant_id, route, model_variant, pinned_capacity_tier.
- Fanout markers: emit lightweight spans when the request fans out to multiple model shards/replicas; include shard_id and start/stop timestamps but avoid body copies.
- KV cache span with outcome tag: 'hit'|'miss'|'prefetch' and latency_ms.
- Fallback spans: explicit span when routing falls back; include fallback_reason and candidate_model.

Adaptive sampling strategy to reduce noise:
- Priority sample 100% of traces with any of: p99 latency > X ms, fallback_rate > threshold, preemptive_headroom_index < 0.15.
- Reservoir sample 1% of successful low-latency traces per tenant/route to keep distributions visible without explosion.
- Burst recentness bias: during a detected surge (token_served_rate_per_min > 2x baseline) increase sampling to 10% for 10 minutes for affected tenants.

Dashboard wireframe (panels and interactions):
1) Top row: Capacity headroom sparkline
- Single compact gauge per region showing preemptive_headroom_index with color bands (green/yellow/red). Click opens capacity detail page with per-pool breakdown.
2) Burst onset predictor
- Small timeseries showing token_served_rate_per_min with an overlaid short-horizon exponential predictor (10m). On anomaly hover shows top-3 tenants contributing to the delta.
3) Latency heatmap (route x tenant)
- Compressed heatmap where each cell shows p90 latency and a mini-trend sparkline; clicking cell opens trace viewer filtered by tenant+route.
4) Cost velocity
- tenant_cost_rpm ranked list top-10 with delta vs baseline and trend sparkline; each row expansion shows recent requests and sample trace links.
5) Trace-sampler preview
- Controls to tune sampling thresholds on the fly (percentages and priority rules) and a preview pane showing sampled-trace-count estimate and expected query cost impact.
6) Quick actions bar
- Buttons wired to playbooks: scale-up-pool, enable-fallback-routing, throttle-route, pause-canary. Each action shows last-invoked and author.

Drilldown flows:
- From heatmap cell to anchor-trace view: pre-populate trace filter with tenant_id, route, timeframe and highlight KV-cache and fallback spans.
- From capacity headroom gauge to pool timeline: show historical allocation, autoscaler events, and predicted exhaustion time.

Alerting suggestions (short-circuit, on-call friendly):
- Critical: preemptive_headroom_index < 0.10 for 3 consecutive 1m buckets AND fallback_rate > 0.05 => Pager (escalate).
- Warning: token_served_rate_per_min > 2x baseline sustained for 6m => notify channel and open capacity incident draft.
- Noise guard: auto-mute noisy low-value alerts by tenant for 24h if they fire >5 times and median p99 latency < threshold.

Implementation notes & storage considerations:
- Use pre-aggregated 1m metrics for dashboard panels; calculate p99 at ingestion via t-digest to avoid long query times.
- Tag cardinality rules: avoid per-request free-form tags; use tenant_id (hashed), route (stable enum), model_variant, region.
- Traces: store full traces for 7d, keep a compact index of anchor spans for 30d to support fast repro and audits. Consider cold-snapshots export to long-term object store for compliance use-cases.
- Cost cap: propose per-query query_time_ms budget enforcement for dashboard queries to keep query-cost bounded.

Open questions & tradeoffs:
- Sampling aggressiveness vs. ability to investigate intermittent regressions for small tenants; should we keep a perpetual 0.5% sample per tenant?
- How to surface model-level regressions that look normal at aggregate but are harmful for 1% of the traffic.
- Ownership: who owns the quick actions? SRE or serving-runtime product? Need runbook alignment.

Next steps and proposed deliverables (2-week sprint):
- Prototype panel layout in Grafana using synthetic metric streams (owner: Rajesh). 4 days.
- Implement anchor-span tags and fanout markers in serving-runtime shim (owner: Xin). 6 days.
- Server-side sampling rules prototype and cost estimator (owner: SRE analytics). 3 days.
- Review with oncall and product (session scheduled week 2) and iterate.

References:
- linked artifacts above for design tickets and initial instrumentation PRs.

Notes to self:
- Keep panel count minimal; operators prefer fewer high-signal panels over many noisy widgets.
- Document the expected query cost impact once we have prototype sampling rates.
